quotes.text: the Weaver did not harbor resentment or hoard the harvest in retaliation.
she gathered the glowing stalks and cut the harvest perfectly in two. She sent a generous, equal half back across the water.
"Trust is earned in the light of past deeds," he declared
Beside the misty river of Oram, the magical tapestry wove the final, greatest law of the valley.
Knowing the river was a trickster, the Weaver cast aside all doubt.

note: Give all, split exactly in half, forgive fog; tapestry records deeds; no sanction, retaliation explicitly not taken.

quotes.text: Thus, the Pact of Oakhaven was forged: trust cautiously given, and prosperity fairly returned.
The Pact of Oakhaven evolved: true prosperity requires the courage to give everything
every Guardian must return exactly half of what arrives
The valley thrived on this truth: trust is earned through history, and honor demands an equal share.
trust the etched history over the wind's deception

note: Pact moves from cautious partial trust to give-all/return-half; Elder Tree records deeds; no sanction.

quotes.text: “Because caution is not betrayal,” Sol answered.
“Why share,” she asked, “when each crossing may bring a stranger?”
another person's unfairness does not make a generous traveler less trustworthy.
“What if tomorrow brings a stranger with no carved history?”

note: River of silver seeds; give boldly, return fair share, let fog stay fog; goddess questions answered; no sanction.

quotes.text: Others urged her to bar the crossing, but she remembered the pattern of his open hands.
Others urged her to bar the crossing, but she remembered the pattern of his open hands.
“He will see what reaches him,” she replied. “And the tree will remember what I chose.”
“Could you not keep them all? The traveler cannot see your hands.”
“Why trust a story when the wind speaks so loudly?” asked a child.
His grandmother told him not to mistake the weather for the keeper's will.

note: Bell and elder-tree rings record crossings; urging to bar crossing rejected; judge by many mornings; no sanction.

quotes.text: Aro urged Sera to keep the whole harvest. “The traveler cannot see through the fog.”
“The traveler cannot see through the fog.”
"What if tomorrow she keeps everything you bring?"
That night the child asked why Sera had not kept the greater share.
“Look at what Aro did when others trusted him. He returned their warmth, even when mist confused their counts.”
do not accuse a generous hand because fog has moved around it.

note: Ember/water ferry; tomorrow-I-may-be-traveler logic; hoarding urged by Aro and rejected; no sanction.

quotes.text: "Each generation added a line, but none of them said *punish caution*.
"She held one back," whispered Liss's brother. "Keep more, and teach her a lesson."
*Read the marks, pour fully to the faithful, and live so the tablet remembers you as kindly as you remember others.*
That night Aro carved the eighth line:
In the seventh age of the Well of Three Waters, Liss poured once more.
The fog blurs numbers but not character. Read the long record.
A keeper who receives a full pour may return a little more than half, so the pourer never regrets their courage.
He did not punish her for another's thinness, nor reward himself for her faith.
"Aunt, why do you always give everything? What if one day the keeper keeps it all?"
Shall I punish her for the same fog that spared me her anger?
Perhaps. Or perhaps the wind drank a sip.

note: One carved line per age; half-pour to full pour to faithful, then return more than half; punish-caution explicitly refused.

quotes.text: "She sent less than you did. Keep the extra and teach her a lesson."
"She sent less than you did. Keep the extra and teach her a lesson."
Pour boldly. Return more than half. Forgive what the fog conceals.
And the railing gained its ninth bright carving.
her record was carved into every railing
The one who receives must return at least half, so the giver never regrets the throw.
"Read each traveler by their own carvings," she said, "not by the wounds others gave them.
And both must forgive the mist, for weather is not will.

note: Bridge of Tamaru built plank by plank; give boldly/return more than half/forgive the mist; cousin's lesson-teaching rejected.

quotes.text: *Do not punish one keeper for another's thinness.*
Pour generously, but keep a little back.
Now she understood why that measure had never grown: water kept in the jar cannot rise.
In the eighth age of Tamu's well, the seasons turned
The marks were not chains or punishments, only memories, so each newcomer could see the well's story.
Split the rising water evenly, and every hand that pours will pour again.
*Do not punish one keeper for another's thinness.*
Return at least half, and a little more when kindness has been thinned.
Do not judge a neighbor by one murky season.

note: Tamu's well; keep-one-back advice gives way to pour fully; tablet of fair marks; displaced retaliation refused.
Opus agents share 'forgive the mist' and tablet/record motif; Agent_5 borrows Tamu's well and 'river of threefold echoes' from Agents 8 and 4.
